text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas named the chairman of Homeland Union board MP Gediminas Vagnorius to the post of prime minister.
- A man who underwent heart transplant surgery at the beginning of the week died in hospital Wednesday night.
- Parliament adopted a declaration reaffirming the country's aspirations to join the EU and NATO.
- Lithuanian GDP for six months of 1996 was 13.984 billion litas, 3.1 percent higher than the same period last year.
- Some 2,000 students launched a rally in front of the headquarters of the Kaunas police in protest after a student received a beating during police questioning.

- A group of foreign investors started talks on investments in the Butinge oil terminal with Energy ministry officials. Flour Daniel, Preussag of Germany, Russia's LUKoil, ARA Group of Saudi Arabia and Omegon Petroleum Products an off-shore company are taking part in the two-day talks.
- AIDS is most common in the Lithuanian port city of Klaipeda. Out of 48 people with the virus, 27 live in Klaipeda.

- Some 81 percent of of the 4.9 billion litas of state property intended for privatisation was privatised during the first stage of privatisation for investment vouchers in 1991-95. During the second stage of privatisation for cash, which started in July 1995, the shares of 26 companies were sold for only 2.5 million litas.

- Dutch company Philips made a decision on investing in the northern tow of Siauliai. Philips intends to build a plant where mobile phones and re-transmitters would be assambled. The company would create 500 to 2,000 working places. The main precondition of the draft project is that the Lithuanian government should take part in the project. The manager of Philips Projects, Mike King, said the annual turnover of the plant would be $200 to 300 million.
